title: MENORA מנורה
concept: Ori Shifrin Anavi is an industrial designer and multidisciplinary visual creator, and a graduate of the Industrial Design Department at Shenkar. His practice operates at the intersection of serial design and material culture, positioned between art and design. Through industrial products, craft, and material experimentation, he explores the presence of objects in public and private space, often using them as raw material for experiential and performative works that invite response and participation.

title: NOT GOOD
concept: This design is a conceptual wordplay that visually references the Israeli lottery, commonly known as "Lotto." To reflect the current atmosphere in Israel, we altered the text from "Lotto" to "Lo Tov," which translates to "Not Good." This ironic twist uses the optimistic lottery logotype to convey a contrasting message. The original Israeli lottery logo was designed by Asher Kalderon in 1968 and was later updated by an unknown designer.

title: EVERYBODY LOVE EVERYBODY
concept: Inspired by the cult scene from Will Ferrell's Semi-Pro where he introduces the concept of ELE - Everybody Love Everybody, we created a 60s-style inclusive illustration. This design reflects the diversity of minorities and personas present in Israeli society, along with a Hebrew translation of ELE. Some elements of the design reference Gush Emunim an Israeli ultranationalist Orthodox Jewish right-wing movement dedicated to establishing Jewish settlements in the West Bank, Gaza Strip, and Golan Heights. We created a satirical version of this, calling it "Gush Metonim," which translates to "The Moderate Bloc" instead of "The Believers' Bloc."

title: BROKEN CROWN II
concept: Keter Group has been an innovative player in Israeli plastic manufacturing since 1948. Not by chance, Keter Plastic is responsible for the Israeli version of a monobloc chair named “Club Chair 2”. Keter’s monobloc plastic chairs share a collective memory associated with funerals, large public events, massive brawls, and more. As a result, monobloc chairs have earned a place of honor in modern Israeli art–used by artists Anna Mirkin, Ori Shifrin Anavi, and more. The hoodie incorporates an image taken by artist and Con board member Neil Cohen.

title: DAVID MELCHIOR INC.
concept: David Melchior was a print manager (aka print producer) that worked in Israel from the mid-’70s to the late ‘90s. In the late ‘80s, David partnered with Jeremy Richman to create the Visual Communication Guide 1989-1990. The book was a professional index for visual communication, a form of Yellow Pages with individual pages of double spread for each professional divided into categories (photographers, graphic designers, advertising agencies, etc). The book is a time capsule commemorating the professionals who operated in the local scene.

title: FUTURE POSTCARDS
concept: Future Postcards visualize a fictional scenario of an Israeli-Palestinian peace agreement. First, the images were created using Ai grounded on reference images and digital compositing by artist Neil Cohen. Then the photos were incorporated into postcard layouts referencing Palphots postcards. Palphot, an Israeli monopoly in printed matter, especially postcards, from 1934 onward, still exists today.

title: END VIOLENCE
concept: Originally released by Pinhas Dagan (MIA) in 1983, this T-shirt is said to have been sent to Menachem Begin, the Israeli Prime Minister at the time. The T-shirt was produced with the naive intent to distribute it all across Israel, hoping it would end the ongoing violence at the time–at least as stated by its creator in “This World” Magazine (העולם הזה) article from 1983.

title: THE FATHER
concept: Edward Bernays was an Austrian-American pioneer considered to be The Father of public relations (also the person who coined the term P.R) and propaganda–sometimes referred to as the "father of public relations”. Bernays was a nephew of Sigmund Freud and used psychoanalytic principles all throughout his work.

title: SYNTHETIC AUTHENTIC
concept: The Synthetic Authentic tee is a design that incorporates memories of a child born in the late 80s coming from a diverse mixture of Moroccan, Libian, and Bulgarian descent and traveling between Israel and the US as a result the divorce of his parents.

title: REALLY FRANK
concept: The H. Berthold Typefoundry, renowned for crafting high-quality typefaces, was founded in 1858 by Hermann Berthold in Berlin. Among being responsible for Akzidenz-Grotesk (released 1896) and considered by many as the mother of all sans serifs, it happens to be that The Berthold Typefoundry is also responsible for the first type specimin–introdocing what is considered as the first modern Hebrew typeface: Frank-Rühl, design by Rafael Frank in 1920.

title: SALE TOTE מבצע
concept:
This design is inspired by a play on words–the Hebrew word for “Sale”. In Hebrew, the word “sale” (mivtza) has two meanings–the first meaning refers to the application in the world of commerce, consumption, and consumerism. The second means “operation” and is primarily associated with military operations–here’s a  long list of them. 
As it turns out, we love sales (mivtzas) of all kinds! Below are some examples of some classic Israeli “sale stickers”, followed by a bunch of commonly used typefaces and letterings meaning “sale”.

title: THE PRICE
concept: Until late 19th century, in most cases, retail goods didn’t have a fixed price. Customers would be expected to haggle with store clerks to get the best price [citation needed]  with the exception of The Quakers, who found it immoral for different customers to pay different prices (now known as price discrimination).

title: ACQUIRED TASTE SOCKS
concept: The Acquired Taste socks pay tribute to the beautiful adaptation of the iconic Coca Cola logo lettering in Hebrew, and Kinley–an orange soda also using the same lettering convention. The sock design incorporates the word “Sale” in Hebrew and English with a typeface inspired by David Tartakover in his famous “Ima” poster from 1987, revived typefaces created by the Fontef Type Foundry.

title: PEACE SOCKS
concept: Peace Socks celebrate the historic The Egypt–Israel peace treaty signed in Washington, D.C. on 26 March 1979, following the 1978 Camp David Accords. The Egypt–Israel treaty was signed by Egyptian president Anwar Sadat and Israeli prime minister Menachem Begin, and witnessed by United States president Jimmy Carter.

title: BETTER FUTURE
concept: Clonex is the Israeli version of Clonazepam (sold under the brand names Klonopin and Rivotril) manufactured by Teva Pharmaceutical. For those unfamiliar, it’s a medication used to help prevent and treat panic and anxiety. This design is a reaction to the polarised public and political atmosphere in present Israel.
